title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: First, define epidemiological intervention parameters. example uses COVID-19 parameters, can adjusted diseases.
code: # Epidemiological parameters (COVID-19 example) n.ind <- 100000  # Large sample for stable estimates TP <- 1.2        # Transmission potential k <- 0.2         # Dispersion parameter (superspreading)  # Vaccination parameters p.vac.idx <- 0.723   # Index case vaccination probability p.vac.sc <- 0.723    # Secondary case vaccination probability vacc.cor <- 0.9      # Household vaccination correlation  # Vaccine effectiveness VE.trans <- 0.4      # Against transmission VE.inf <- 0.72       # Against infection  # Region for household sizes (or use hh_probs for custom) region <- "NSW"  # Epidemiological distributions (COVID-19 defaults) # For other diseases, adjust these: inc_meanlog <- 1.63   # Incubation period meanlog inc_sdlog <- 0.5      # Incubation period sdlog gi_meanlog <- 1.376   # Generation interval meanlog gi_sdlog <- 0.567     # Generation interval sdlog  # TTIQ scenarios to evaluate the.scenarios <- c("optimal", "partial", "baseline")  # Isolation durations to evaluate quarantine.durations <- c(14, 7)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: Use test.designs() systematically generate valid testing schedules:
code: # Maximum possible test days max_days <- max(quarantine.durations)  # Minimum spacing between tests (e.g., 2 days) min.space <- 2  # Generate all schedules with 1, 2, or 3 tests all.times3 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 3,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  all.times2 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 2,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  all.times1 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 1,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  # Combine all schedules all.times <- all.times3 %>%   filter(Var1 <= 5) %>%   add_row(     all.times2 %>%       mutate(Var3 = Inf) %>%       filter(Var1 <= 5)   ) %>%   add_row(     all.times1 %>%       mutate(Var2 = Inf, Var3 = Inf)   )  nn <- nrow(all.times) print(paste("Evaluating", nn, "testing schedules"))

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: Now loop isolation durations TTIQ scenarios, evaluating testing schedules parallel:
code:
results_list <- list()  for (hq.d in quarantine.durations) {   for (ts in the.scenarios) {      cat(paste("
Evaluating", ts, "scenario with", hq.d, "day isolation
"))      # For 7-day isolation, filter out schedules that extend beyond day 7     if (hq.d == 7 && ncol(all.times) == 3) {       all.times_filtered <- all.times %>%         select(-Var3) %>%         distinct() %>%         filter(Var1 <= hq.d & (Var2 <= hq.d | is.infinite(Var2)))       nn <- nrow(all.times_filtered)     } else {       all.times_filtered <- all.times     }      # Step 1: Run base simulation (once per scenario/duration combination)     set.seed(1)  # For reproducibility     CQ.output <- CQ.sim2(       n.ind = n.ind,       TP = TP,       k = k,       p.vac.idx = p.vac.idx,       p.vac.sc = p.vac.sc,       vacc.cor = vacc.cor,       VE.trans = VE.trans,       VE.inf = VE.inf,       quarantine.duration = hq.d,       the.scenario = ts,       region = region,       inc_meanlog = inc_meanlog,       inc_sdlog = inc_sdlog,       gi_meanlog = gi_meanlog,       gi_sdlog = gi_sdlog     )      # Step 2: Evaluate all testing schedules in parallel     cl <- makeCluster(4)  # Use 4 cores (adjust based on your machine)     registerDoParallel(cl)      tic <- Sys.time()      output <- foreach(       i = 1:nn,       .combine = rbind,       .packages = c("tidyverse", "isolatr")     ) %dopar% {       CQ.sim.test.times(         CQ.sim.output = CQ.output,         n.ind = n.ind,         test.times = all.times_filtered[i, ] %>% as.numeric(),         TP = TP,         VE.trans = VE.trans,         the.scenario = ts,         gi_meanlog = gi_meanlog,         gi_sdlog = gi_sdlog       )     }      toc <- Sys.time() - tic     cat(paste("Completed in", round(toc, 2), attr(toc, "units"), "
"))      stopCluster(cl)      # Combine schedules with results     results <- cbind(all.times_filtered, output) %>%       mutate(         scenario = ts,         q.duration = hq.d       )      results_list[[paste(ts, hq.d, sep = "_")]] <- results   } }  # Combine all results all_results <- bind_rows(results_list)

code: # Clean up column names colnames_base <- c("t1", "t2", "t3") if (ncol(all.times) <= 3) {   colnames(all_results)[1:3] <- colnames_base[1:3] }  # Add number of tests all_results <- all_results %>%   mutate(     t2 = case_when(       is.na(t2) ~ Inf,       TRUE ~ t2     ),     t3 = case_when(       is.na(t3) ~ Inf,       TRUE ~ t3     )   ) %>%   mutate(n.tests = 3 - is.infinite(t2) - is.infinite(t3))  # Identify optimal schedules optimal_schedules <- all_results %>%   group_by(scenario, q.duration, n.tests) %>%   filter(IPq == min(IPq)) %>%   mutate(TT = paste0("(", t1, ",", t2, ",", t3, ")")) %>%   mutate(TT = gsub(pattern = ",Inf", replacement = "", x = TT)) %>%   select(scenario, q.duration, n.tests, TT, IPq, sdIPq, mean.cases)  print(optimal_schedules)

code: near_optimal <- all_results %>%   group_by(scenario, q.duration, n.tests) %>%   arrange(IPq) %>%   mutate(efficiency = IPq / min(IPq)) %>%   filter(efficiency <= 1.02) %>%   mutate(     T1 = paste0(min(t1), "-", max(t1)),     T2 = paste0(min(t2), "-", max(t2)),     T3 = paste0(min(t3), "-", max(t3))   ) %>%   mutate(     T2 = gsub("Inf-Inf", "-", T2),     T3 = gsub("Inf-Inf", "-", T3)   ) %>%   select(scenario, q.duration, n.tests, T1, T2, T3, efficiency) %>%   distinct() %>%   arrange(desc(q.duration), desc(n.tests))  print(near_optimal)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: simulation models following process close-contact communicable disease: Index case infection: individual (primary close contact) exposed pathogen Incubation period: Time exposure symptom onset Contact tracing: Index case identified isolated Household transmission: Potential spread within household isolation Testing schedule: Active testing may detect infection early Passive detection: Symptom development leads healthcare seeking Onwards transmission: Undetected infections may cause tertiary cases key question: many tertiary infections occur undetected secondary cases?

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: number secondary cases index case ii follows negative binomial distribution: ncases,∼NegBin(k,TP)n_{cases,} \sim \text{NegBin}(k, TP) : - TPTP = transmission potential (mean) - kk = dispersion parameter (smaller = overdispersion/superspreading)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time infection index case infection secondary case jj: GIij∼LogNormal(μgi,σgi)GI_{ij} \sim \text{LogNormal}(\mu_{gi}, \sigma_{gi}) Default parameters (COVID-19): μgi=1.376\mu_{gi}=1.376, σgi=0.567\sigma_{gi}=0.567, giving median GI ≈ 3.96 days. parameters configurable via gi_meanlog gi_sdlog diseases: - Influenza: μgi≈0.91\mu_{gi} \approx 0.91, σgi≈0.52\sigma_{gi} \approx 0.52 (~2.5 day median) - SARS: μgi≈2.0\mu_{gi} \approx 2.0, σgi≈0.45\sigma_{gi} \approx 0.45 (~7.4 day median)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time infection symptom onset index case ii: IPi∼LogNormal(μip,σip)IP_i \sim \text{LogNormal}(\mu_{ip}, \sigma_{ip}) Default parameters (COVID-19): μip=1.63\mu_{ip}=1.63, σip=0.5\sigma_{ip}=0.5, giving median IP ≈ 5.1 days. Configurable via inc_meanlog inc_sdlog: - Influenza: μip≈0.34\mu_{ip} \approx 0.34, σip≈0.42\sigma_{ip} \approx 0.42 (~1.4 day median) - SARS: μip≈1.39\mu_{ip} \approx 1.39, σip≈0.51\sigma_{ip} \approx 0.51 (~4 day median)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Household size index case ii region rr: HHi,r∼Fr(h)HH_{,r} \sim F_r(h) Fr(h)F_r(h) empirical CDF household sizes region rr. Built-data covers Australian states. Custom distributions can provided via hh_probs region worldwide.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Index case vaccination status: Vi∼Bernoulli(pvac,idx)V_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_{vac,idx}) Secondary case vaccination (household members): Vij∼{CorrelatedBinary(Vi,ρ)household memberBernoulli(pvac,sc)otherwiseV_{ij} \sim \begin{cases} \text{CorrelatedBinary}(V_i, \rho) & \text{household member} \\ \text{Bernoulli}(p_{vac,sc}) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} ρ\rho household vaccination correlation.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Probability infection given exposure: P(infection∣exposure)=(1−VEtrans⋅Vi)⋅(1−VEinf⋅Vj)P(\text{infection} \mid \text{exposure}) = (1 - VE_{trans} \cdot V_i) \cdot (1 - VE_{inf} \cdot V_j) : - VEtransVE_{trans} = effectiveness transmission (reduces infectiousness) - VEinfVE_{inf} = effectiveness infection (reduces susceptibility) parameters can represent vaccine effectiveness, prior immunity, protective factors.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Secondary infections classified based timing relative isolation: Pre-isolation (tinf<tisot_{inf} < t_{iso}): Occur index case quarantined Household (tiso≤tinf<tiso+Qdurationt_{iso} \leq t_{inf} < t_{iso} + Q_{duration}): Occur quarantine household members Post-quarantine (tinf≥tiso+Qdurationt_{inf} \geq t_{iso} + Q_{duration}): Occur quarantine ends proportion pre-isolation post-quarantine infections randomly reassigned household (probability hh_transmission_prob, default 0.5), household size limit. accounts uncertainty exact infection timing location.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Test sensitivity varies viral load, changes infection course. model sensitivity using logistic function: Let CC = time peak viral load (days symptom onset): C=min(IP,3.5)⋅U(0,1)C = \min(IP, 3.5) \cdot U(0,1) U(0,1)U(0,1) uniform random variable. Time since infection test tt: st=tiso+t−1−IP−Cs_t = t_{iso} + t - 1 - IP - C tt test day (relative isolation start). Test sensitivity: P(positive∣infected,t)={11+exp(−(β0+βpre⋅st))st<0 (pre-peak)11+exp(−(β0−βpost⋅st))st≥0 (post-peak)P(\text{positive} \mid \text{infected}, t) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-(\beta_0 + \beta_{pre} \cdot s_t))} & \text{} s_t < 0 \text{ (pre-peak)} \\ \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-(\beta_0 - \beta_{post} \cdot s_t))} & \text{} s_t \geq 0 \text{ (post-peak)} \end{cases} Default parameters (calibrated COVID-19 PCR): - β0=1.5\beta_0 = 1.5 (intercept) - βpre=2.2\beta_{pre} = 2.2 (pre-peak slope) - βpost=0.22\beta_{post} = 0.22 (post-peak slope) can adjusted via test_intercept, test_slope_prepeak, test_slope_postpeak different test types (e.g., rapid antigen tests) diseases.

text: testing schedule 𝐭=(t1,t2,…,tn)\mathbf{t} = (t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n): Calculate sensitivity pip_i test time tit_i Simulate test results: Ri∼Bernoulli(pi)R_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_i) First positive test: tfirst=min{ti:Ri=1}t_{first} = \min\{t_i : R_i = 1\} (∞\infty negative) Add turnaround time: tfirst+TTATt_{first} + T_{TAT} Add delays: tfirst+TTAT+Tothert_{first} + T_{TAT} + T_{} : - TTATT_{TAT} = test turnaround time (scenario-specific) - TotherT_{} = interview + notification delays (scenario-specific)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: typical workflow consists three steps: Simulate transmission dynamics using CQ.sim2() Evaluate testing strategies using CQ.sim.test.times() CQ.sim.notest() Compare results across different strategies

title: Quick Start Guide
text: First, simulate transmission 1000 index cases (primary close contacts) isolation: output data frame one row per secondary infection:
code: set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility  # COVID-19 example with default epidemiological parameters sim_results <- CQ.sim2(   n.ind = 1000,                  # Number of index cases to simulate   TP = 3.0,                      # Transmission potential (mean secondary cases)   k = 0.25,                      # Dispersion (lower = more superspreading)   p.vac.idx = 0.7,               # Probability index case is vaccinated   p.vac.sc = 0.7,                # Probability secondary cases are vaccinated   vacc.cor = 0.8,                # Household vaccination correlation   VE.trans = 0.5,                # Vaccine effectiveness against transmission   VE.inf = 0.7,                  # Vaccine effectiveness against infection   quarantine.duration = 14,      # Isolation period (days)   the.scenario = "optimal",      # TTIQ scenario   region = "NSW"                 # Region for household size distribution ) head(sim_results)  # Check infection types table(sim_results$who)

title: Isolation Simulation for Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: n.ind Integer. Number index cases (primary close contacts) simulate. TP Numeric. Transmission potential - mean number secondary cases per index case (analogous R0 fully susceptible population). k Numeric. Dispersion parameter negative binomial distribution secondary cases. Lower values indicate greater overdispersion (superspreading). p.vac.idx Numeric. Probability index case vaccinated (0-1). p.vac.sc Numeric. Probability secondary case vaccinated (0-1), non-household contacts. vacc.cor Numeric. Correlation coefficient (0-1) vaccination status within households. Higher values mean household members likely vaccination status. VE.trans Numeric. Vaccine effectiveness transmission (0-1). Reduces probability vaccinated index case transmits infection. VE.inf Numeric. Vaccine effectiveness infection (0-1). Reduces probability vaccinated secondary case becomes infected. quarantine.duration Numeric. Duration quarantine/isolation period days. .scenario Character. TTIQ scenario name. Must one : "optimal", "partial", "baseline", "current_nsw_case_init" (deprecated alias baseline). .state Character. Deprecated, use region instead. region Character. Region name household size distribution. Default "NSW". See abbreviate_states valid Australian values. Ignored hh_probs provided. hh_probs Numeric vector. Custom household size probabilities sizes 1-8+. Must sum 1 length 8. provided, region ignored. inc_meanlog Numeric. Mean incubation period distribution log scale. Default 1.63 (COVID-19, ~5.1 day median). inc_sdlog Numeric. SD incubation period distribution log scale. Default 0.5 (COVID-19). gi_meanlog Numeric. Mean generation interval distribution log scale. Default 1.376 (COVID-19, ~3.96 day median). gi_sdlog Numeric. SD generation interval distribution log scale. Default 0.567 (COVID-19). hh_transmission_prob Numeric. Probability pre-isolation infection occurs within household (vs community). Default 0.5.

title: Isolation Simulation for Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: function implements stochastic simulation model disease transmission isolation/quarantine. model: Samples individual-level characteristics (vaccination, incubation period, isolation time, household size) index case Samples number secondary cases negative binomial distribution Samples generation intervals (time successive infections) lognormal distribution Classifies infections occurring isolation, within household quarantine, post-quarantine Models household-correlated vaccination status Calculates passive detection times based TTIQ scenario Filters infections based vaccine effectiveness function uses lognormal distributions incubation period generation interval.
